name: Satis Beach House, Great Ocean Road Linen provided
description: Satis is a cosy, quirky and comfortable beach shack with a large, private tea-treed garden.  Our house is so close to the inlet, beach, shops, lighthouse and cliff walk. No view, no spa, not a glass box but fun and games for all!  Welcome to Satis, which means 'enough' in Latin.  And it is.
neighborhood_overview:
Aireys Inlet is a beautiful bush hamlet by the sea. Nature abounds from the fantastic Fairhaven surf beach to the calm inlet and numerous little bay beaches with rock pools and rugged cliffs.

The Great Otway National Park abuts the town and a variety of walking tracks allows you to explore the rainforest in all seasons.

Cafes, a pub and restaurants and numerous shops are low key and high quality. The elegant White Queen, a slender lighthouse, can be seen for miles along The Great Ocean Road.

“For whatever we lose (like a you or a me),
It's always our self we find in the sea.”

e e cummings

And check out my guidebook and extra information sheet for tips on Aireys Inlet.
host_about:
We live on a broad acre cropping, sheep and alpaca farm on the Wimmera plains, enjoying the space, people, environment and the ability to grow our own produce. 

Our beach house on the Great Ocean Road and our city apartment are a wonderful contrast to life on the farm. 

Satis Beach House is comfortable, quirky and just around the corner from a beautiful surf beach, estuary and cliff top walks along the coastline of south eastern Australia.  Excellent cafes, restaurants, a bookshop, galleries, surf club and pub add to the coastal mix at Aireys Inlet.

Greyfriars is an iconic mid century apartment block with a lovely central garden in St Kilda East, Melbourne.  This sweet one bedroom apartment is our city ‘pied à terre’ and we love it.

As travellers, we appreciate comfortable beds, good linen, clean spaces and many small details that make a stay into a holiday.  We hope you will find these simple luxuries in our places.

Contact Fiona for bookings for either of these spaces, or check us out here and @satisbeachhouse and on @riparide.

We offer you the opportunity to stay in our fully equipped, private, purpose built, Apartment at the rear of our home. Suitable for 4 adults, 1 child, 1 infant. In the coastal village of Queenscliff, only 1.5hrs from Melbourne, with easy access to the Great Ocean Road.
Your hot tub, set in the privacy of the rear garden & sunset from the adjacent walking path.
Easy walk to Harbour, local shops/restaurants, Blues Train & beach. Comfy beds, quality linen & continental breakfast all included.
neighborhood_overview:
There is so much to see and do in Queenscliff that you really need to consider staying a few nights. All guests comment that they wish they had more time to extend their stay here in this beautiful coastal town. Queenscliff is full of history and has an abundance of beautiful old buildings to explore. The Maritime Museum, Historical Museum, South Wharf, Historical Railway and Queenscliff Fort offer a glimpse into the history of the area.
If you would prefer to spend the day exploring the great shopping or restaurants on offer, then you are also spoilt for choice. There are great bike and walking paths on offer for you also
Or consider visiting the local wineries. Share a 'taste platter', enjoy some of the regions best wines and take in the incredible views and hospitality of the area.
host_about:
My husband and I love living in Queenscliff.  We’re retired and spend time volunteering in our community.  
We manage Swan Bay Views in Queenscliff, suitable for 1 or 2 couples or small families. 
The area has such incredible history and amazing beauty, we love to share the information with you - if you're interested!  
We are also extremely good at leaving our guests to their own devises, should you wish to explore and experience on your own.

name: Eighty Nine West Anglesea
description: Light-filled 3BR, 2 bathroom beach house that sleeps 8 (2 queens + 4 singles). Comfy, modern and easygoing—just a short walk to the beach, shops and Surf Coast Walk. Open year-round and perfect for families, kids and pets too. A lovely spot to relax and unwind.
neighborhood_overview:
Nestled in a peaceful pocket of Anglesea, Purnell Street offers a tranquil retreat just moments from the town's vibrant heart. This quiet, family-friendly street is ideal for those seeking relaxation and a genuine coastal experience.

A short stroll takes you to Anglesea's main beach, the river, local shops, and cozy cafes.

For nature enthusiasts, the Surf Coast Walk is mere meters from the front door (approx 100m), offering stunning cliff-top views, beach access, and winding bushland trails for all kinds of walkers, runners, and cyclists..

The area is renowned for its natural beauty, with the Anglesea Heath and Coogoorah Park offering opportunities to explore diverse flora and fauna. Golfers might enjoy a round at the local course, where kangaroos often graze on the fairways.

Whether you're here to surf, hike, or simply unwind, Purnell Street serves as a perfect base to enjoy all that Anglesea has to offer.
host_about: Based in Bendigo, we love having a property in Anglesea that we can go to, to unwind and relax. Mostly, so my young boys can get to know the beach - as they spend most of their lives surrounded by mountains. My favourite thing to do is run along the Surf Coast Walk trail to Point Addis, and do this as often as I can. You can expect a relaxed approach to hosting from me, Eighty Nine West is definitely our happy place - we sincerely hope it will be yours too :)

neighborhood_overview:
Torquay is iconic Victorian surf town with magnificent beaches. It is the birthplace of some famous surf wear brands with retail outlets for Rip Curl, Quicksilver, Billabong, Oakley and Roxy.

Each year at Easter nearby at Bells Beach the famous Rip Curl Pro surfing championship is held.

Torquay is a gateway to the Great Ocean Road, one of the world's most scenic coastal drives. Cruise the Great Ocean Road to the Wye River General Store and Cafe for lunch and stop and see kangaroos at Anglesea, koalas at Lorne and some stunning surf breaks, lookouts and waterfalls signposted along the way.

Go a little further and admire the superb coastline along the Great Ocean Walk near Apollo Bay. Stop and visit the Cape Otway lighthouse, the Otway Fly Treetop Walk and the magnificent tall timber rain forest nearby at Triplet Falls. Take time to stop and enjoy fine dining, the local wines and fresh produce.

host_about:
YOUR HOST: GARY COPOLOV 

Hello, my name is Gary and I live in Middle Park, Melbourne.

I currently manage over twenty inner bay side short to long term accommodation properties located in Middle Park, Albert Park, South Melbourne, Port Melbourne, St.Kilda, Balaclava, Elwood and even one property in North Carlton and Torquay.

Those in the "hood" know that these locations are arguably some of Melbourne’s best and most desirable inner-city suburbs. I believe I am fortunate to live and manage properties in the area and to meet and host so many wonderful guests. 

My Airbnb hosting journey started when my wife, Jo and I bought Florence Court in Nimmo Street, Middle Park in 2015. It is a heritage listed, mid 30's Art Deco apartment block in where I now offer four fantastic short term accommodation apartments. I now operate sixteen brilliant short to long term accommodation properties in the area ranging from apartments to houses and from one to four bedrooms. They are all stunning and fitted out to the very highest standard. 

As an Airbnb Superhost I offer my guests a concierge like service. I am an unashamed ambassador for the area where I have lived for over 30 years. Just tell me your interests and I will offer my recommendations. 

Each property has a copy of "Adventures" which provides details my recommended local To Do's and the very best of nearby dining pleasures. There are many recommendations for guests of all ages. 

My wife, Jo and I met playing tennis at Kooyong Lawn Tennis Club and were married in Paris just over 28 years ago. Jo is a part time teacher at the local primary school where she is a special education reading teacher. She has a real passion for books, real estate and interior design. A typical week will see her at a local café with friends, walking our dog in the nearby park, seeing a movie, attending her book club, doing a yoga class or shopping for the next thing for one of the properties we fitout and list on Airbnb. 

We have two children, Louis and Natasha. Natasha (Tash) is a Project Co-ordinator in the construction industry. When she is not out socialising or getting away for the weekend, she may occasionally walk our friendly Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever called Hudson. We love pets and welcome them at all properties. 

Our son Louis lives in Portland, Maine, USA where he works for the Boston Celtics basketball team as Player Manager of the G League Maine Celtics.  He attended university in Boston, USA and represented Australia in rowing as a coxswain. 

On weekends, given a chance, Jo and I visit a beach side get-away apartment with stunning sea views in Torquay, just over an hour’s drive from Melbourne. Torquay is Victoria's surf capital and the gateway to the famous Great Ocean Road. The apartment is available for stays on Airbnb. (Sleeps 8). In Torquay, we enjoy walks, great local food, wine, the many surf beaches and the company of friends. 

We have travelled to Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and the USA where we have enjoyed Airbnb hospitality in England, France, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria, Croatia, Turkey, Netherlands, Denmark, Sweden and the United States. I wish to share that same pleasure and the excitement of travel with my guests. 

I am a self-employed Marketing Consultant whose consultancy, Gold Medal Marketing develops and implements winning business development programs for businesses in various industries. I have written and delivered a number of business development programs. 

When not hosting, I am working hard as the honorary Chairman of the Australian Patients Association (APA) which advocates, educates and supports Australian patients. The APA strives to be the voice of and for Australian patients. 

I regularly attend a local gym for regular workouts which I am pleased to introduce to my active guests. 

On weekends in Winter, I watch St. Kilda, an Australian Rules Football Club as a long standing and sadly long-suffering club supporter and member.

With a family of building designers, I am always working on some property development or creative project for myself, family or and friends or for the property owners that I represent. 

I like to catch a movie or show and visit galleries and believing that you should “be a tourist in your own town” try get out and about to something interesting either near or far. 

I look forward to sharing the many great properties which I manage and my local experience with my guests. 

I am always available to ensure that property owners are well served by my services and that guests have a great stay. 

Yours, 

Gary Copolov.

name: Great Ocean Road Sunrises
description: You'll feel energised, catching the sun rise over the sparkling ocean as you lift your head off the downy pillow in this new-build, luxurious & bright, beach studio. Stroll 200m to the beach, wander along to Lorne's iconic Swingbridge Cafe for great coffee and food, or doze back to sleep – the choice is yours.
neighborhood_overview:
Lorne is the heart of the Great Ocean Road. It’s nestled on the shores of Louttit Bay and has a unique environment where beach meets rainforest (the Otways). The mountains surrounding Lorne form a distinctive micro-climate which brings unique flora and fauna to the region, as well as some of the world’s best walking trails. Spend a few days wandering in Lorne and you're sure to spot Kangaroos, Koalas, Cockatoos, Parrots, Wombats and Echidnas.
The protected bay waters are perfect for all types of activities - Swimming, surfing, snorkeling and ski paddling are amongst the most popular.
The range and quality of restaurants and cafes right on the beach and along the main street will be sure to satisfy almost every taste.
If you're a shopper - get excited and prepare to be tempted by the amazing options for clothes, shoes, jewellery, award-winning ice cream and an end-of-day cocktail.
host_about:
We are foodies who juggle a bit of fitness with relaxing with a beer or a vino rosso.
We love travelling to see new amazing places and meeting friendly local people.

We are a couple who have migrated  to Apollo Bay and also Australia in September 2014..  so not quite locals yet ;-)  We love the relaxed  and friendly life Apollo Bay has to offer for both young and older. We  enjoy meeting so many interesting people by hosting on here and to think we had never heard of it until late 2014  and started hosting in April 2015  Since then it has been non stop!
We are amazed everyday at the interesting people from so many countries that pop in and out of our lives while on their adventures, travels and  quiet  nights away from the hustle of the city .

host_about:
WHY I WANT TO HOST 
I LOVE to Travel. My passion for travel originally started when I was a sixteen and headed to Sweden on student exchange.  At the age of 21 I left Australia to return to Sweden to work as an au-pair.  I stayed for another year before heading to Ireland where I remained for 9 years. During those 9 years I made it a priority to travel as much as possible through Europe, Africa, USA and Asia.
For the last five years I have shifted my priorities to saving and purchasing my first home. I now live in my home town (born and breed) Geelong which is the second largest city in Victoria after Melbourne which is only a short hours drive away.  Geelong is also perfectly situated at the beginning of the Great Ocean Road.
Of all the great places that I have visited, it was local people who allowed me to experience a place and gave me the best tips and recommendations. I would now like to do the same for guests in my home.

ABOUT ME
I’m a young (ish), fun loving, friendly, outgoing, active female. I love to have fun and travel.  I have been lucky enough to be able to visit over 38 countries for extended periods. I am very health conscious and I do my best to eat well, and stay active: Netball, Tennis, Running, etc. I have many people I consider friends all over the world and I do like making new friends when possible. Often people ask me which country did I enjoy the most and I can’t answer that:  from the bright lights and fantastic shopping of New York, to the mud huts and simplicity of Africa to the beautiful beaches of the Caribbean I just love all the experiences other countries offer. My motto is you only live once! so try everything!

host_about:
WHY I WANT TO HOST 
I LOVE to Travel. My passion for travel originally started when I was a sixteen and headed to Sweden on student exchange.  At the age of 21 I left Australia to return to Sweden to work as an au-pair.  I stayed for another year before heading to Ireland where I remained for 9 years. During those 9 years I made it a priority to travel as much as possible through Europe, Africa, USA and Asia.
For the last five years I have shifted my priorities to saving and purchasing my first home. I now live in my home town (born and breed) Geelong which is the second largest city in Victoria after Melbourne which is only a short hours drive away.  Geelong is also perfectly situated at the beginning of the Great Ocean Road.
Of all the great places that I have visited, it was local people who allowed me to experience a place and gave me the best tips and recommendations. I would now like to do the same for guests in my home.

ABOUT ME
I’m a young (ish), fun loving, friendly, outgoing, active female. I love to have fun and travel.  I have been lucky enough to be able to visit over 38 countries for extended periods. I am very health conscious and I do my best to eat well, and stay active: Netball, Tennis, Running, etc. I have many people I consider friends all over the world and I do like making new friends when possible. name: Resort Style 5 Bedroom Home in Old Torquay
description:
Fully renovated, 5 bedroom plus 3.5 Bathroom within the heart of old Torquay. Walking distance to beaches, parks, cafes, restaurants, supermarkets and surf shops. Located on a 1200m2 block it offers lots of privacy and security.
Our place is great for families (with Kids), big groups, and furry friends (pets outside only).
*** No Schoolies or Team end-of-season trips ***
neighborhood_overview:
Torquay is a vibrant seaside resort town, located only 95km south west of Melbourne, it is the official start of the Great Ocean Road. Attracting thousands for its modern lifestyle, great beaches and surf culture.

Torquay is home to many surf clothing and surf equipment stores including Rip Curl, Quiksilver, Billabong, Globe and Strapper Boards . You will also find a blend of cafés, restaurants and convenient takeaway outlets, ice creameries, hotels and restaurants. You can even learn to surf at one of the famous surfing schools. Boutiques and galleries are dotted around Torquay, there is something for everyone.

Nestled in a quiet and leafy part of Old Torquay, our home is a great base for those who are after a quiet escape with friends and family, or seeking some adventure, it's where the coast and hinterland meet - the options are endless and you'll want to come back to stay for years to come.
host_about:
We are a professional couple with two young children. We work hard, but we love to spend our leisure time with family and friends, eating great food and travelling the world.

With European background, we have spent many summers travelling through Europe, where we love to enjoy the sun, shopping, and most of all the amazing variety of food! And we're always up for an impromptu trip to Hong Kong, Singapore, even LA, as a quick couple's getaway, or a fun family adventure with friends.

Recently, much closer to home, we discovered a love for Torquay, with it's friendly community, amazing beaches and incredible sights all within a short distance. This led us to buy and renovate a house in Old Torquay, with all the best of the area at our doorstep.

Our focus in hosting is comfort and meeting your needs for a relaxed holiday.  It is now our principle place of residence and more of a family home that we share for special guests.

We've renovated our 80s home with 2 modern bathrooms and laundry, fully equipped kitchen and a wonderful living environment inside and outside.   Anglesea is on a pretty river that runs through the town to the spectacular Surf Beach.  Another beach more suitable for families is at Point Roadknight.  It's a 15-20 minute walk to the main beach, surf club and shops or 5 mins by car.

Our home adjoins the 18th Fairway of the famous Anglesea Golf Course with its many kangaroos and bird life!  If you love photography and walks, surfing and swimming, come and enjoy our sanctuary.  We've 2 lovely balconies for just chilling out with a drink or a good book and an outdoor Balinese shower complete with hot water!  Our large daybed and window seat provides an ever changing view to life on the golf course complete with kangaroos!

Melbourne's freeways and Geelong Bypass make it an easy drive to Anglesea with no traffic lights en route!

host_about:
A mother, a partner, a gardener, an artist and a proud property owner of Pips on Bank and Pips on Mitchell. 
I love Port Fairy.....  it is my 'breathing space' and I feel an instant calm and belonging when I visit.  Similarly, Bendigo is filled with early adulthood memories of fun times and being such a friendly accessible city.  
I love coffee and late breakfasts; I also love to discover glimpses and moments that sometimes we're prone to walk past.  I find other people’s artwork fascinating and would have a gallery in my home if I could!  This influences how I decorate and hope that the visual interest is evident in abundance in each property. Of course, comfort is another factor that is important as we regularly use each accommodation ourselves and expect to feel at home when we do.
I am a thinker and talker and a lover of people therefore the sharing of my little cottage and the funky loft apartment comes naturally in that I want people to ponder and enjoy the spaces and experiences as I would.
My partner is a potter and together we are Oxart Pottery.   Our handmade functional ceramics are used in the properties and should you enjoy them or want to purchase the same, please contact me or check out our website.

name: The Bank Koroit
description:
Come and enjoy a beautiful, relaxing space; rich in Western Victorian history and culture.
Koroit is the beating heart of Victoria's, if not the centre of Australia's Irish heritage.
An 1870 building with all the modern appointments you can enjoy. Your own private apartment is upstairs with its own entrance and access to the a beautiful back garden.

But it is Undoubtedly a heritage experience of Western Victoria. Nothing beats a football match at the oval in season. Nothing beats a cricket game in season and the the bowling club is always ablaze. Afterwards, there's always a fun night out at the local pubs.
Australian Music always pops up here; especially at Crossley Hall; just out of town. Local, national and even international artists can show up.
All that aside, there are heaps of cottage business pop ups all over the place to entice the wanderer about the town. Whatever your interests; drive about the area and you'll find history, antiques, op. shops, organic spuds, fresh eggs and all sorts of local produce.

neighborhood_overview: A very quiet neighborhood in this historic country town of Coleraine in the Southern Grampians.  Whether you want to visit for a relaxing escape or explore the region. Check out the website: visitgrampians/coleraine.   The township of Coleraine is of historical significance (history dating back to 200 years) it is one of the oldest permanent urban settlements in the Grampians Shire.  It is of architectural significance as a planned town including a typical range of buildings including public facilities and utilities, churches, commercial buildings and private residences. Of further architectural significance is the range of fine architect designed buildings which date from the late nineteenth century on Whyte Street.  Enjoy stepping back in time in this old 1940’s cottage in this beautiful old country town.
host_about:
We love to travel and also love old country towns and  country houses with rich history and character.  We have a busy life style in Melbourne and enjoy family time and travelling when we get a chance to escape from work.  We find the cottage relaxing and cosy.  It sets us back in time and is located in the most beautiful  country town of Coleraine in the Southern Grampians.  There is history around every corner of Coleraine for those who are eager to learn its fascinating past. It is one of the oldest country towns in Victoria with a settled history dating back almost 200 years.  In fact, the local cricket club claims to be the second-oldest continuously playing cricket club in the world. The area was first settled by Europeans in 1838 for pastoral grazing.  

Coleraine is a great spot which can be used as a base to travel to many beautiful destinations around the Grampians and Victoria but also to South Australia, the blue lake is approximately an hour away from the cottage.  

 We hope you enjoy it as much as we love it!

name: Corsair Cottage, beach over the road
description:
Classic beach house in a great spot.
The beach opposite is great for kids & dogs, so bring them both.
Stroll the dog beach to Queenscliff or the seaside boulevard to Point Lonsdale. Maybe you’d rather meander through the moonahs of ‘Lovers Walk’ or follow the shores of Swan Bay.
Look for dolphins as you swim or snorkel, then rinse off in the outdoor shower.
Enjoy a BBQ whilst the kids and dog explore the secure yard. End the day in the outside bath under the stars, listening to the ocean.
neighborhood_overview:
Corsair Cottage is situated in between Point Lonsdale and Queenscliff, two beautiful small coastal towns on the Bellarine Peninsula.

Point Lonsdale has both an ocean beach (great for surfing) and a sheltered beach stretch of beach which extends to Corsair Cottage. It is known for its relaxed vibe and boutique shops, cafes and restaurants. It also has a 18 hole golf course close to town.

Queenscliff is a historic maritime town with heritage architecture at the entrance to Port Phillip Bay. You'll find historic pubs and a large variety of shops, cafes and restaurants. From Queenscliff you can take the ferry across to Sorrento. Or you may choose to stay on this side and ride along the magnificent 'rail trail' adjacent to Swan Bay (the rail trail is only a few hundred metres from Corsair Cottage!). Perhaps you'd rather enjoy some music on the famous Blues Train or indulge in some local food and wine on the Q train all well taking in the beautiful local scenery.

Skenes Creek is located in The Otways where you can find some of Australia's best rainforest scenery in the Otway Ranges amongst tall trees, ancient plant life and lush ferns. The following local attractions are highly recommended: Marriners Lookout, Cape Otway Lighthouse, The Telegraph Station and WWII Radar Station, Maits Rest Rainforest Trail, Erskine Falls and Otway Fly Treetop Walk. Of course, you should not miss the Twelve Apostles along the Great Ocean Road.

description: Laze about in your breezy bush meets the ocean, colourful and cheery space.  A two minute drive or 15 minute downhill stroll to the magnificent Pt Roadknight beach. Anglesea/Point Roadknight nature and neighbourhood...
Our property is in quiet, leafy part of Anglesea. Your accomocation is a 20 minute downhill stroll to the exquisite Point Roadknight beach and a 5 minute amble to the fabulous walking, running and mountain bike tracks of the Anglesea Heath – part of the Great Otway National Park and the richest and most diverse vegetation community in Victoria. Jump into your car for a 2.5km drive to Anglesea town & shops. A 30 minute, spectacular cliff top walk or low tide beach walk will get you to the Anglesea shops, restaurants, surf hire and finest gelato on the Surf Coast.

It’s a great base to explore all the Great Ocean Road has to offer – safe swimming, brilliant surf spots, paragliding launches, road and mountain biking, walking/running tracks, Twelve Apostles and the many sporting, music and other events happening along the Great Ocean Road.
host_about: Mum of two, wife, mature-age PhD student, lover of fresh air, outdoors and adventure. We're both fairly well travelled - I lived in Africa for several years involved in an outdoor adventure company followed by several years filming alternative sport and wildlife documentaries. The kids are an energetic and happy duo and are currently into Vikings and icecream, icecream, icecream.  We love sharing our knowledge of the area and really happy sharing our family home with travellers.  Hope to meet you soon.

neighborhood_overview: This beach-side retreat is ideally located within walking distance to all the great attractions of Historic Queenscliff. It is only one hundred meters or so to buy fresh fish off the boat at the Marina or a little further for coffee, fish and chips and fine dining. Steam train rides for the kids or blues music nights for the adults are a stones throw away. You can easily walk to the beach, the famous market,  the Maritime Museum, the Ferry, the beautiful Lighthouse Reserve and the main street of Historic Queenscliff. For the more adventurous, kayak across Swan Bay or take a boat trip across the treacherous Port Phillip Bay heads. Alternatively, swim with the dolphins, snorkel at Popes Eye or take a scuba diving course nearby.

description:
"CHI pronounced as chē, means the vital life force or the balance of energy."

Chi B&B is at the heart of the Great Ocean Road and one of the only stops on the Great Ocean Walk that is only meters away from track. Surrounded by the rolling hills of Glenaire, Aire River and just down the road from Castle Cove Beach and Lookout, you will “Find your Chi” by indulging your senses, allowing you relax, revitalize and take a long healthy breath.

You are WELCOME at Chi B&B.
neighborhood_overview: There is plenty to see and do around Chi B&B, Glenaire. After a gourmet breakfast, indulge in a gentle walk on Castle Cove beach, explore the beautiful Aire River West area, or venture out for a day trip to the local waterfalls of the Great Otway National Park, Cape Otway, or the world famous Twelve Apostles. The native flora and fauna abounds here, which is a great opportunity to see Black Cockatoos, Eastern Grey Kangaroos, Black Swamp Wallabies, sleepy koalas and waddling echidnas in their natural habitat. During the winter months you might be lucky to sight the whales during their winter migration.

host_about:
I am an active, healthy 61 year old. Love people, travel, animals, tennis, gardening, dancing, singing,  yoga,  creative arts, and anything fun. Spontaneous, genuine and caring. I have travelled widely both to Asia and Europe. neighborhood_overview: Kennett River is best described as a hamlet - with Kafe Koala General Store offering great food (burgers, pizza, fish & chips, grab and go meals, locally roasted coffee and basic supplies. Next to the beach in a quiet side street this 4 bedroom house offers everything for a relaxing weekend away or an extended stay over winter with both gas heaters and in built wood burning fire in the living areas.

neighborhood_overview:
Our home is set in a quiet residential street directly across from steps leading through the dunes to the beach. The Cheeky Cow Cafe is a 10 minute walk, great for morning coffee, breakfast or lunch. A further 5 minute walk is to the Ocean Grove Hotel and Bistro which has a great menu in its spacious and often busy restaurant, which also has great activities including in-ground trampolines for the kids.
Two major shopping areas (Shell Road shopping centre and The Terrace shopping strip) within 1-2 kms and while walkable ( 20 -30 minutes) if you are shopping best to drive, as there is a hill. Plenty of parking at both venues. Both have major supermarkets as well as bakery's, butchers, chemists.

The main street or The Terrace shopping strip also has lots of shops for browsing as well as cafe's and several restaurants including Thai, Chinese , Indian and of course great fish and chips!

name: Relax at Ironbark views
description:
Relax and enjoy the Best that the coast has to offer.
Expansive views in a modern family friendly home located just minutes walk from Fairhaven beach. Two Large decks to choose from, enjoy a BBQ or Relax outside on the Comfy Outdoor Lounge whilst soaking up the sun.
There is plenty of entertainment with an Olympic trampoline (use at your own risk), Cubby House and even a Basketball Tower to practice your shooting skills. Large enough to accommodate two Families.

description:

description:

description:
"Kennebec" homestead is all yours! We have lovingly restored (& added a bit of modern luxury) this 1902 homestead which was build by our great grandfather. Located 13km from Dunkeld, the southern gateway to the Grampians, and 20km from Hamilton.

"Kennebec" now offers the homestead which sleeps 6, the "Family Studio Suite" which sleeps 4 & our beautiful studio space which is perfect for brides getting ready, large family gatherings or workshops/crafting weekends with your friends.
neighborhood_overview:
We are located in the heart of south west Victoria near the gorgeous Grampians. There are no shortage of places to see and explore during your stay including:
• Dunkeld and the Grampians
• Byaduk caves
• Wannon & Nigretta falls
• We are at the centre of the largest volcanic plain in the Southern Hemisphere - Kanawinka Geopark [you fill find more information in our guest book]
• Mount Eccles National Park

You are also centrally located with Port Fairy & Portland 100km, Warrnambool 100km & Mount Gambier, with its picturesque Blue Lake, 135km.

name: Seacroft Room 15 - King Bed - AMAZING LOCATION
description:
Seacroft is a former historic Monastery and Seminary on the Great Ocean Road with stunning 180 degree ocean views of Cape Patton and Apollo Bay.
Room 15 - king bed - ocean out the window.
Set in beautiful gardens surrounded by green farm land and views to the State Forest.
Conveniently located on the Great Ocean Road 13 minutes prior to Apollo Bay that has shops, cafes and restaurants.
Shared modern toilet and shower facilities.
Sleep with the sound of the ocean.
Up to 16 rooms available.
neighborhood_overview:
There is a secluded beach right across the road with amazing volcanic rock pools to explore, swimming holes in the rocks that warm up during the day and a sandy little beach. There is also a spectacular 45 minute walk from Seacroft to the Carisbrook Waterfalls.

We are situated in a place of natural beauty. Looking East we have spectacular views of Cape Patton and the State Forest climbing up over the hills. Looking West we have views all the way along the coast to Apollo Bay and beyond.

name: Holiday Retreat in Rustic "Old Lonsdale"
description:
Enjoy a fabulous coastal break among the tree tops at our holiday home in rustic "Old Lonsdale", only a 15 minute walk to the front beach and the Pt Lonsdale village, or to the surf beach on Ocean Road.

Breakfast in the morning sun on our north-east facing front balcony, and relax in the evening with a beautiful sunset over Lake Victoria from our west facing balcony. Our recently completed renovations include a rebuilt kitchen and bathroom, and new windows and carpets in the bedrooms.
neighborhood_overview:
Our street is a quiet tree-lined street located on the bayside of Fellows Road, and offers a beautiful walk through the best streets of "Old Lonsdale" to both the Point Lonsdale village and front beach, and to the surf beach and lighthouse on Ocean Road. We are also very close to the Lonsdale Golf Course on the Geelong side of Fellows Road. Our golf course is currently being rebuilt with a new course layout and an incredible new clubhouse with sunset views over Lake Victoria - visitors always welcome.

A number of Wineries and their restaurants are only a short drive away. The ones we like are Banks Road, Basil's Farm, Scotchman's Hill, Jack Rabbit and Terindah Estate. The last two have fantastic views across the Bay.

Queenscliff, with all its attractions, is either a 5 minute drive by car, or a very pleasant bike ride on an off-road track, partly along the beach. You can also ride your bike along the Bellarine Rail Trail (off-road through the local country-side)

description: You’re going to love the location of this very comfortable beach shack just 450 meters to beach, shops and all that all Lorne has to offer. The lounge room and upper deck have expansive water views. There are four bedrooms, sleeping up to ten guests, two bathrooms and two separate living/dining areas. neighborhood_overview:
Lorne is situated in a delightful bushland setting. The beach and shops are only a short walk away; no need to take the car anywhere. The township has a large variety of shops and restaurants as well as a cinema. There is even a large swimming pool, several spas, a gymnasium, mini golf and trampolines located on the beach front. The beach itself is wide and clean and fully patrolled in summer months.
There are numerous walks around Lorne and the information booklet contains details of many of them. The local golf course and tennis courts are only a ten minute drive away. The golf course is open to everyone and has a public dining area with spectacular coastal views. There is a huge variety of wild life around Lorne, and koalas, kangaroos, and brightly coloured king parrots are often spotted. Lorne is often referred to as a place where the bush meets the sea..and it truly is.

neighborhood_overview:
The beautiful township of Nelson is situated on the pristine Glenelg River where the river estuary and mouth meets the great Southern Ocean. The surrounding Lower Glenelg National Park is full of wild natural beauty with accessible and friendly walking tracks and amazing birdlife.

Nelson is perfectly situated for leisurely day trips along the rugged Limestone Coast. Experience the beauty of the famous volcanic Blue Lake in Mount Gambier or Mount Schank. Wine lovers can take a day trip to the world famous Coonawarra. World famous cave diving is also a hidden gem.

description:
Torquay is a popular beach destination year round, a gateway to the Great Ocean Road and surrounds.
Our Home is comfortable and pet friendly with all amenities required for an stress free enjoyable stay. We are located in the quiet ‘old’ part of Torquay across the road from Whites (beautiful dog friendly) beach with walking and biking tracks leading to town centre about 2km away. neighborhood_overview: The house is on a dual occupancy site located at the rear of the block. We are located in a very quiet street and close enough to the beach that you hear the waves on some days.
host_about:
About 6 years ago after spending wonderful summers in Torquay a friend and I were given an opportunity to buy a place that was too good to refuse purely because of its proximity to the beautiful Torquay beach. Busy lives with family and work commitments in Melbourne meant that it would be some years before either of us would get the opportunity to spend the time we would have liked to in our little place so we opted for full time rental. 
Circumstances changed and in 2017 we decided that we would now both in a position to come to Torquay more often and the house would no longer be rented long term.  We received received the keys from the real estate agent mid October and embarked on renovating the whole place with the assistance of local tradies, friends and YouTube. A lot of love, sweat, pain and tears has gone to what has now become our dream holiday home. 
We both love coming to Torquay and spend a lot of time walking along the beach, visiting cafes and shops, pottering around the garden and sourcing lovely homewares.  
We approached in February 2018 by a friend to rent the home for a couple of weeks, while at first we were reluctant we agreed to give it a try and placed the house on Airbnb. We have had a few bookings, the guests have been great, the whole experience and the feedback has been very positive, any money we make we use to buy beautiful things that we hope our family, friends and guests will use and also love.

As the largest holiday accommodation provider in Port Fairy and surrounds, we the team at Hearn’s Port Fairy Accommodation are your holiday rental specialists. With 130+ holiday rental properties, we offer the broadest range of holiday accommodation options in Port Fairy.

Whether you are looking for a luxury home or villa with ocean views; a central historical cottage; a romantic retreat; an apartment overlooking the beautiful Moyne River; a luxurious suite with pool; a comfortable beach shack or even that something quirky or a little bit different – the Hearn’s team will help you find and settle into accommodation your needs and budget. All you will need to do is relax and enjoy the lifestyle of this iconic seaside village.

Located along the magnificent Great Ocean Road, Port Fairy is a quiet enclave on the edge of the dramatic Southern Ocean. Soak up the historic charm of this bluestone fishing village, learn about Port Fairy’s rich maritime history, be enchanted by the heritage listed bluestone cottages or wander up to the historic Port Fairy Lighthouse on Griffiths Island.

Walk the wide open street with a fresh coffee in hand and find a handmade treasure at one of the many artisan boutiques. Take your time over brunch, lunch or dinner at one of our many cafes and restaurants and sample the region’s produce.

Indulge the romance of the wooden boats bobbing along the picturesque Moyne River or take a long afternoon meander along the boardwalk. Take a long stroll along the iconic East Beach or explore secluded beaches and rock pools along the shores of South Beach.

There is nothing better than fresh air, good food and nature to nourish the body and soul! Port Fairy is the perfect retreat!

Contact the team today – your Port Fairy holiday awaits you.

description:
Welcome to our much loved home away from home!

This modern 2-storey mezzanine townhouse is quietly located at the rear of the historic Cora-Lynn complex right in the centre of Lorne.

This townhouse features a beautiful treed outlook from all its windows and two small balconies. As the front beachbox, it is the only one featuring a westerly outlook, attracting lots of beautiful natural light throughout the day.

Perfect for a romantic getaway or small family holiday. Location can't be beat.
neighborhood_overview:
The Great Ocean Road along Victoria's western coastline is world renowned for its beauty and Lorne is often described as the jewel of this Surf Coast. Located on the edge of beautiful Loutit Bay, the town nestles between the blue ocean and the Otway National Park. Lorne has been a popular holiday spot since Victorian times when the journey from Melbourne would take several days, but today, with the new Geelong by-pass, the journey can be made in less than 2 hours.

Lorne has something to offer everybody

- beautiful, safe, patrolled, family friendly beaches
- magnificent National Parks
- 4-wheel drive trails, bush walks
- surfing, wind-surfing, para-gliding, fishing, golf
- swimming pool, trampolines, skate park
- adventure playground and BBQ's on the foreshore
- cinema
- cafes, restaurants, bars, alfresco dining
- spa and beauty salon at the Mantra Resort

host_about:
WHY I WANT TO HOST 
I LOVE to Travel. My passion for travel originally started when I was a sixteen and headed to Sweden on student exchange.  At the age of 21 I left Australia to return to Sweden to work as an au-pair.  I stayed for another year before heading to Ireland where I remained for 9 years. During those 9 years I made it a priority to travel as much as possible through Europe, Africa, USA and Asia.
For the last five years I have shifted my priorities to saving and purchasing my first home. I now live in my home town (born and breed) Geelong which is the second largest city in Victoria after Melbourne which is only a short hours drive away.  Geelong is also perfectly situated at the beginning of the Great Ocean Road.
Of all the great places that I have visited, it was local people who allowed me to experience a place and gave me the best tips and recommendations. I would now like to do the same for guests in my home.

ABOUT ME
I’m a young (ish), fun loving, friendly, outgoing, active female. I love to have fun and travel.  I have been lucky enough to be able to visit over 38 countries for extended periods. I am very health conscious and I do my best to eat well, and stay active: Netball, Tennis, Running, etc. I have many people I consider friends all over the world and I do like making new friends when possible. Often people ask me which country did I enjoy the most and I can’t answer that:  from the bright lights and fantastic shopping of New York, to the mud huts and simplicity of Africa to the beautiful beaches of the Caribbean I just love all the experiences other countries offer. My motto is you only live once! so try everything!

Vita and Fabian

description: Our pet friendly cottages are on 5 beautiful acres of natural bushland between the magnificent Great Ocean Road and renowned surfing location, Bells Beach. A stay at Bells Beach Cottages any time of the year will ensure a comfortable relaxed holiday along the Great Ocean Road.

name: Wensley - Rustic Luxury, Great Ocean Rd Hinterland
description:
Set high on the rolling hills of 80 acres The Wensley is a bespoke timber, architectural house built from recycled Oregon and Ironbark. The Wensley is a haven of peace and serenity in a secluded but central pocket of the Surf Coast Hinterland called Wensleydale - offering you a chance to chill out and stay put or explore The Great Ocean Road and surrounding countryside with complete privacy.

1.5 hrs from Melb, 20 Mins Birregurra & Brae, 25 Mins Aireys Inlet , 15 mins from Moriac & Winchelsea
neighborhood_overview:
Wensleydale is the Gateway to the Otways & The Great Ocean Road. There is so much to explore and do. Whether it's close to home - or further a field.
WALKS
1) You can walk to the back of the property and climb the fence into state park. And take a look around. There are old dirt bike trails in there you can explore - however given it's so hot this week you will be watching your step without boots.

2) You can walk easily enough down Casboults road and explore around there without worrying too much about snakes. I'll be surprised if you see one but they are around.

3) Further A field are these walks in the Otways Erskin Falls is a good one for a day trip. https://www.visitotways.com/walks-and-waterfalls/

4) One of my favourite walks is down by the clifftop at Aireys Inlet (20 mins drive) - if you go to the lighthouse at Split Point https://goo.gl/maps/Kmnv97NsxcecmeKXAthere's a coastal path that leads off the carpark and down alongside eagle roc

name: Fad's Surf Shack, where the forest meets the sea
description: Fad's Shack is a one bedroom surf shack at the foot of the Otway Ranges in the tiny seaside town of Kennett River on the Great Ocean Road. The shack has one bedroom (1 queen bed and 1 single bed), a kitchen/living area, a bathroom, and a deck with sea views.  It is set on the edge of the forest and has many birds, kangaroos, and koalas. Enjoy the tranquility of this tiny seaside hamlet.  Walk to the pristine beach or visit the local waterfalls and temperate rain forests and tree fern glades.
neighborhood_overview: Kennett River is a coastal hamlet at the foot of the Otway Forest.  There is one shop, about 50 houses, and a population of 41.  The beach is gorgeous, and the river is a safe place for kids to paddle.  Wildlife is abundant and tame.  Walks in the forest to access waterfalls are well signed and not too strenuous.  There’s a guide book of local walks on the bookshelf.  Fad’s Shack is a 500m (8 min) walk from the beach.  Kick back, relax and enjoy.
host_about: I am a Professor in malaria research at Melbourne University.  I teach premedical biology, marine biology and evolutionary biology.  I'm interested in surfing, making wooden surfboards and 1950s American cars.  I'm married with four independent adult children.

Built c 1854 as a coaching station, an addition was built in c1876 - this section is now available for guests.
The apartment sleeps up to 4 adults with a queen sized bed in a separate bedroom, as well as a very comfortable queen sized sofa bed in the huge lounge area.
There is a fully equipped kitchen also full separate laundry.
There is an electric 'log fire' heater as well as split systems in both the lounge and bedroom.
Free wifi and built-in USB charger.
neighborhood_overview: Coleraine has a fabulous history which can be explored easily.  We are located in a beautiful valley surrounded by magical countryside.  Take a walk beside the creek.  In the summer months we have an open air swimming pool that is open to the public for free!
host_about:
Retired after many years in the community development industry.  I enjoy meeting new people and hearing about their travels. Love the garden and presently working on reinvigorating a large space that has been sorely neglected over the years!  Our home is the oldest surviving building in Coleraine, and was originally a staging station  between Adelaide and Melbourne where horses and travellers could rest for the night.  I love social history, and this home and this little town satisfies my interest!  I've been an amateur writer for many years - and have been working on a novel for almost 30 years, but family, work and other commitments have always been in the way.  Maybe now that life has slowed down a little, I'll have the time to finish it!
In my younger days, I was lucky enough to travel extensively - I worked in the travel industry for twelve years in the 'dream job', before leaving to start a family.  My favourite destination is Spain, the food, the colour and the people make it fun and exciting.  However, Australia has to be one of the most amazing countries in the world as far as quality of life, freedom of choice and spectacular wide open spaces, and I feel extremely lucky that I live here.
I love cooking and entertaining - the whole process of planning, shopping, preparing, cooking and serving is something I find truly rewarding.  Spending time with friends and family is precious and something none of us should take for granted.
I'm a lucky woman.

name: Wongaburra Woolshed
description:
Wongaburra is a private horse farm on 618 acres, close to aboriginal art sites and walking trails - 1 hour from the Hall's Gap tourist precinct.

We have two accom options for guests:

Our converted Woolshed which is completely self contained with full kitchen/dining/studio bedroom/2 showers/verandah with views/woodfire/gas bbq/aircon. (BYO food)
Our farmhouse guest wing which offers 2 private bedrooms/1 bath/shower/toilet plus lounge. Breakfast supplied. (Tea/coffee/toast/cereal/fruit)
neighborhood_overview: We are a rural community and are very proud of our local town of Cavendish.  There is a cafe and general store the historic 'settlers walk' along the Wannon River and cemetery, police station, primary school, community hall and ANZAC memorial.  Local events include the 'Fleece and Flower' show, and bi-annual 'Redgum Festival'.  Our local pub is owned by a co-op of local people, and the chef is renowned returned local James Campbell (raised here in Mooralla)
host_about:
"We opened Wongaburra as a horsemanship centre late in 2007.  We run horsemanship clinics and camps and enjoy sharing our property with others from all over Australia and around the world. We decided to create a B&B for guests and have been renovating our farmhouse in readiness.  We look forward to sharing our very special part of Australia with new guests, and offer a unique experience with horses, mountains, ancient redgums, kangaroos and emus as our backdrop".  - Justin and Christine Corbidge 
Chris is a horsewoman with 30 years teaching experience, who travels across Australia and OS. Justin (also a horseman) is  'house husband', property manager and main caretaker. The care and development of Wongaburra has been a shared 'labour of love' for both of them since they fell in love with the property and purchased it in late 2006.

We love sharing our area with travellers from all over the world. This is our paradise as my husband calls it and we welcome you :)

host_about:
As the largest holiday accommodation provider in Port Fairy and surrounds, we the team at Hearn’s Port Fairy Accommodation are your holiday rental specialists. With 130+ holiday rental properties, we offer the broadest range of holiday accommodation options in Port Fairy.

Whether you are looking for a luxury home or villa with ocean views; a central historical cottage; a romantic retreat; an apartment overlooking the beautiful Moyne River; a luxurious suite with pool; a comfortable beach shack or even that something quirky or a little bit different – the Hearn’s team will help you find and settle into accommodation your needs and budget. All you will need to do is relax and enjoy the lifestyle of this iconic seaside village.

Located along the magnificent Great Ocean Road, Port Fairy is a quiet enclave on the edge of the dramatic Southern Ocean. Soak up the historic charm of this bluestone fishing village, learn about Port Fairy’s rich maritime history, be enchanted by the heritage listed bluestone cottages or wander up to the historic Port Fairy Lighthouse on Griffiths Island.

Walk the wide open street with a fresh coffee in hand and find a handmade treasure at one of the many artisan boutiques. Take your time over brunch, lunch or dinner at one of our many cafes and restaurants and sample the region’s produce.

Indulge the romance of the wooden boats bobbing along the picturesque Moyne River or take a long afternoon meander along the boardwalk. Take a long stroll along the iconic East Beach or explore secluded beaches and rock pools along the shores of South Beach.

There is nothing better than fresh air, good food and nature to nourish the body and soul! Port Fairy is the perfect retreat!

Contact the team today – your Port Fairy holiday awaits you.

host_about:
Hi!I started traveling internationally in 2014.  Yeah, I know, it's a bit late to start but hey, at least I started.  I hope to make up for the lost time in the coming years and I am looking forward to Airbnb to help me achieve my dream of setting foot to all the continents of the world.

I don't like traveling alone and I usually travel with my best friend.  She makes sure that I try the local cuisine while I'm in charged of the art and cultural experiences.  Our traveling style complements each other.

When I look at places to stay, I usually gravitate to places with really great-looking bathrooms. A luxurious-looking bathroom upgrades any room in my mind.  What makes a great bathroom in my book?  Of course, very clean with complete and in good working order facilities (the shower has water, the sink drains do not have rust, etc).  I wouldn't even care if there are no complete toiletries as long as the bathroom looks good.  I bring my own toiletries, anyway.

Why do I travel?  Not to escape but to see how wonderful our world and the people in it are.  And to rejuvenate.  After a trip from somewhere, my trust and faith in people are restored and I begin to see the place from where I originated with new eyes.  This makes this life more exciting to live.

As of this year, 2015, my top 5 places to see are:
1) Siem Reap, Cambodia (done in 2016)
2) South Korea (done in 2017)
3) Morocco
4) Russia
5) Turkey

name: Stone Keepers Run-Riverfront historical homestead
description:
An historical pastoral homestead, established in 1850's, set right on the banks of the Hopkins River.
The weatherboard home and converted bluestone dairy has seven bedrooms, most with ensuite, and several living areas. This large, but intimate home, has enough space for the whole family or for a couple wanting to experience a secluded rural retreat.
Stone Keepers is close to Warrnambool at the end of the Great Ocean Road.
It has abundant bird life, fauna and unique views of the river.
neighborhood_overview:
Stone Keepers Run is situated on 4 acres of rural land in a beautiful natural setting on the banks of the Hopkins River. The Great Ocean Road is a few kilometres up the road, with the Twelve Apostles being 60 kms away.
Port Fairy is located 30 minutes away
The Otway National Park is 100kms
'Tooram Stones' are located right outside our front gate and mark the spot where tidal and fresh water meet. 'Tooram', an indigenous word, means good fishing. This special fishing spot is renowned locally as one of the best places to fish. Trout, Bream and Perch, right out the front gate.
Located a few minutes from the Allansford township and 10 minutes to Warrnambool.
We are close to Logans Beach, where whale watching during the winter months is very popular and Warrnambool's spectacular coast line.

name: On the edge of Rocklands Reservoir, 4 bedroom home
description:
On the far side of the Grampians, nestled in stringy bark bushland on the edge of Rocklands sits Yangoora.
Once home to farmers, bee keepers, rose growers and tree changers, now yours to enjoy.
Settle on the deck as the red necked wallabies shyly appear and native birds splash and natter in the coolness of the birdbath.
Kayak the clear water, try your hand at catching a fish or wander the dirt track to explore and be captivated by the bush.

host_about:
As the largest holiday accommodation provider in Port Fairy and surrounds, we the team at Hearn’s Port Fairy Accommodation are your holiday rental specialists. With 130+ holiday rental properties, we offer the broadest range of holiday accommodation options in Port Fairy.

Whether you are looking for a luxury home or villa with ocean views; a central historical cottage; a romantic retreat; an apartment overlooking the beautiful Moyne River; a luxurious suite with pool; a comfortable beach shack or even that something quirky or a little bit different – the Hearn’s team will help you find and settle into accommodation your needs and budget. Soak up the historic charm of this bluestone fishing village, learn about Port Fairy’s rich maritime history, be enchanted by the heritage listed bluestone cottages or wander up to the historic Port Fairy Lighthouse on Griffiths Island.

Walk the wide open street with a fresh coffee in hand and find a handmade treasure at one of the many artisan boutiques. Take your time over brunch, lunch or dinner at one of our many cafes and restaurants and sample the region’s produce.

Indulge the romance of the wooden boats bobbing along the picturesque Moyne River or take a long afternoon meander along the boardwalk. Take a long stroll along the iconic East Beach or explore secluded beaches and rock pools along the shores of South Beach.

There is nothing better than fresh air, good food and nature to nourish the body and soul! Port Fairy is the perfect retreat!

Contact the team today – your Port Fairy holiday awaits you.

description:
Welcome to our gorgeous seaside villa located front row on the iconic Great Ocean Road within the beautiful township of Apollo Bay, Victoria.

neighborhood_overview:
Beach Break is situated front row on the Great Ocean Road. It's a short 5 minute walk into town or a brisk 8 minute walk along the beach to the harbour for fish and chips. You can pretty much leave your car in the carport and walk everywhere during your stay.

And can I also say that we have gorgeous neighbours in the other three apartments behind Beach Break. Both couples (one couple owns two - the apartment directly behind Beach Break is for their adult children to stay in occasionally) are semi retired and really lovely people so if you see them out the front feel free to say hello. host_about:
Hello my name is Penny. Matt and I have owned Beach Break for just over 13 years. 
We've enjoyed so many holidays in Apollo Bay over the past 30 years and actually had our honeymoon staying at Beacon Point way back in 1990.

Buying Beach Break was a serendipitous moment. We just happened to be in the right place at the right time and the bank said yes (still pinching myself about that!) Looking back I think it was meant to be and we've loved every minute of turning Beach Break into our own little seaside escape and styling it so that others can enjoy it as well.

This place is full of so many wonderful memories for our family.

We hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

Best wishes for now
Penny x

Soak up the historic charm of this bluestone fishing village, learn about Port Fairy’s rich maritime history, be enchanted by the heritage listed bluestone cottages or wander up to the historic Port Fairy Lighthouse on Griffiths Island.

Walk the wide open street with a fresh coffee in hand and find a handmade treasure at one of the many artisan boutiques. Take your time over brunch, lunch or dinner at one of our many cafes and restaurants and sample the region’s produce.

Indulge the romance of the wooden boats bobbing along the picturesque Moyne River or take a long afternoon meander along the boardwalk. Take a long stroll along the iconic East Beach or explore secluded beaches and rock pools along the shores of South Beach.

There is nothing better than fresh air, good food and nature to nourish the body and soul! Port Fairy is the perfect retreat!

neighborhood_overview:
Nelson is a small fishing and holiday town located on the Glenelg River, just 4 kilometres east of the state border with South Australia and around 70 kilometres north-west of Portland.

Nelson's town centre includes a hotel, general store, roadhouse and a visitor information centre. The river flows through the town centre and there are scenic parks, jetties and boat ramps along the river banks.

Cruise operators offer informative trips along the Glenelg River for visitors, and well worth experiencing is the journey through the 15 kilometre limestone river gorge with cliffs up to 50 metres high rising on both sides of the river.

As the Glenelg River heads south of Nelson's town centre, it empties into Oxbow Lake which then has an outlet into the Southern Ocean. There are sandy beaches along the lake shore and at the river mouth which offer sheltered swimming. Swimming is not advised at the ocean beach due to dangerous undertows.

name: The Wren's Nest - Forrest
description: Immerse yourself in the natural beauty of the Otway Ranges with a stay at The Wren's Nest. Located centrally in the picturesque town of Forrest, our two bedroom cottage offers a perfect getaway for couples, families or small groups of friends. Spend your days enjoying mountain bike riding, bush-walking, waterfall gazing, fabulous food, wine and locally crafted beers and your evenings relaxing on the back deck watching the sunset, enjoying a massaging spa bath or lazing by the fire in a recliner.
neighborhood_overview:
Our favourite things to do in Forrest and surrounds are:
Lake Elizabeth - follow the well worn track to the tranquil Lake Elizabeth and enjoy being surrounded by majestic gum trees and lush ferns. See if you can spot some platypi!
Stevensons Falls - walk the easy trail to the waterfall, wander amongst the giant redwood trees, climb on the rocks around the waterfall and dip your toes in on a warm day. A great place for a picnic.
West Barwon Reservoir - take a walk along the creek (look out for the koala’s) or through Fern Gully to view the impressive reservoir.
Bike Riding - explore the many picturesque mountain bike riding tracks that surround Forrest - there is something for all ages and abilities starting from the kid-friendly (and very fun) mountain bike practice trail and pump tracks in town right up to a range of high intensity trails. And if you are not a bike-rider, walking some of these trails is a fabulous way to experience being immersed in nature.
Ye

description:

Each cabin has majestic with views of lush green farmland, rain forest and onto passing ships in the Southern Ocean.
While, at the bottom of our garden you’ll find the Old Beechy Rail Trail, and a secluded rain forest.
By night, you can view the local glow worms or perhaps the greatest light show of all, the Milky Way.

Spend the day at the beach or sit at the cafes and watch the ships enter and exit Port Phillip bay. The front beach is inside the bay and perfect for kids. Walk around the lighthouse and explore the rock pools at low tide.

There is a small supermarket which can cater to all your needs and a short drive away is Queenscliff with restaurants and hotels.

Located just a few doors from the front beach and shopping precinct with it's wonderful eateries, IGA and gallery plus the children's park, bowls club and surf riders club nearby.

neighborhood_overview:
The popular surf town of Ocean Grove lies roughly 30 minutes’ drive east from Geelong. Nestled on the spectacular Bellarine Peninsula, it’s surrounded by pristine beaches, acclaimed wineries and golf courses making it a vibrant holiday hotspot. Try surfing at Ocean Grove main beach or stand-up paddle boarding at nearby Barwon Heads.

Follow one of the region’s many scenic walking trails that range from the peaceful tracks within the Ocean Grove Nature Reserve to the challenging 32-kilometre Bellarine Rail Trail. Get your caffeine fix at Parade Espresso Bar, dine with a view at the relaxed waterfront eatery The Dunes and pick up pies and sweet treats from Rolling Pin Pies and Cakes. Don’t miss a visit to nearby Oakdene Vineyards Cellar Door for a seasoned wine tasting within its historic 1920’s homestead.

name: Warrnambool District - The Studio at Heathbrae
description:
The Studio at Heathbrae is situated 1.5 km from the charming Irish village of Koroit. Located halfway between Warrnambool and Port Fairy, surrounded by beautiful green countryside, walking distance to Tower Hill reserve and a short drive to the hidden gem of Killarney beach.
The studio is a private apartment, semi attached to our home, Heathbrae, in peaceful gardens set on over 2 acres.
neighborhood_overview:
'The Studio at Heathbrae' is situated in a semi-rural zone 1.5 km's from the historical town of Koroit.
Koroit is a quaint Irish Heritage township offering all amenities and eateries including traditional fare at the famous Mickey Bourke's Hotel, fine dining at Izzy's restaurant, Asian quisine at Little Thaihouse restaurant and tapas at the trendy Noodledoof Craft Brewery & Distillery.

The Tower Hill State Game Reserve is within walking distance and a nature lover's delight for young & old. You are guaranteed to see kangaroos & emus at dusk and even a koala or two if you look up among the gumtrees.

The beautiful beaches of the Great Southwest Coast of Victoria are a short drive away, with our closest being the safe, secluded beach at Killarney taking only 8 mins. If you like to be a bit more adventurous with a boogieboard or surfboard, then East Beach at Port Fairy of The Main Beach at Warrnambool are for you.
host_about: My wife Laurisanne,  and I have lived in the South West over the last 25 years and look forward to meeting new people. We love our rural setting and are happy to share our space and tranquility. I am a keen golfer, enjoy travelling and exploring. Laurisanne loves gardening and you may see her out in the garden where she is at her happiest. We look forward to welcoming you to our home.

name: Original 1960's Family Beach House
description:
Bring the whole family to this happy place with lots of room for fun. Close to beautiful beaches, this three bedroom beach house has been renovated to include modern amenities with a classic feel.
Ample parking, including a double carport that's tall enough for your boat, and a securely fenced yard to keep your pooch safely on the property.

neighborhood_overview:
Indented Head is an idyllic hidden bayside gem on the Bellarine Peninsula. The crystal clear shallow waters of Half Moon Bay are perfect for swimming, kayaking, stand up paddle boarding and snorkeling around the wreck of the Ozone paddle steamer just off the beach. Small boats, SUP boards and kayaks can be hired from one of the quaint boat sheds on the beach.
Safe, calm beaches that are perfect for children to explore. Indented Heads is a very popular spot for boating, fishing and sailing with an excellent boat ramp, the Peninsula is also very popular for cycling & golf. The Bellarine Peninsula is also home to many fabulous wineries, restaurants, lovely cafes, farmers markets, golf courses and even a Whiskery, producing excellent whiskey and gin. If you are so inclined, Adventure Park (water park, open Oct-April) is located on the Peninsula, about 20 mins from the beach house, and is a fun day out! Indented Head is very dog friendly, and a great spot for walks & beach swims with
host_about: Hi, my name is Fran and I live on the beautiful Bellarine Peninsula with my husband, three young children & our mini schnauzer. My husband & I have brought this original 60's beach house back to life ourselves over several years & this has been a project filled with love and great family times. Our beach house in Indented Head holds such wonderful memories and it is our hidden little escape from the busyness of the world. It is a place where we find we can really switch off & relax and our children & dog enjoy endless hours of outdoor play & exploring, often only seeing them when they are hungry! Many an afternoon & evening has been enjoyed relaxing & eating meals on the large deck, taking in the sunsets & the stars. We have always found that Indented Head is a place that is truly beautiful all year round. The warmer months are filled with beach time, and in the cooler months there is nothing more enjoyable, especially on the sunny clear days, than to rug up and go for a walk, exploring the beach collecting shells & other washed up treasures. Of an evening, in the warmer or cooler months, sitting outside looking up at the abundance of stars we can see down here, whilst enjoying the ambience of the fire pit, is the perfect unwind...& our children always love the toasting of marshmallows that comes with the fire pit being alight! description: Beach retreat ~ ‘Mosey’ along the iconic Great Ocean Road, one of the world’s most scenic coastal drives, and stop here to be inspired by the magnificent ocean views from the first floor apartment windows that span all the way from Torquay to Jan Juc. Continuing to let the life adventures unfold...

neighborhood_overview:
Port Campbell is a beautiful little seasonal beachside town. It is located in one of the more remote parts of the Great Ocean Road so be prepared before you arrive, especially in the colder months.

You will find most businesses open most days/nights during the shoulder and peak seasons (Nov-April). You can expect a very quirt scene during the off season (May-Oct). This is the beauty of Port Campbell, a space to sit back and really unwind amongst the rugged Great Ocean Road.

The town offers a small general store but if you are here for a few days then I recommend you pick up supplies from the surrounding towns/cities before you come. During the peak season you will find cafes opening at around 8am and restaurants serving food until approximately 10pm. In the cooler months these cafes and restaurants generally open later and close earlier.

Lorne has been a popular holiday spot since Victorian times when the journey from Melbourne would take several days, but today, with the new Geelong by-pass, the journey can be made in less than 2 hours.

neighborhood_overview:
Portarlington is a historic coastal township located on the Bellarine Peninsula, 28 km from the city of Geelong, in the state of Victoria, Australia.

Portarlington is a popular holiday destination, offering sheltered swimming beaches and an attractive foreshore featuring a pier, BBQ and picnic areas, and a large camping area. The town's main commercial centre is on Newcombe Street and is dominated by the landmark Grand Hotel which was built in 1886. Parks and recreation reserves occupy the sloping foreshore between the shops on Newcombe Street and the beach, providing good views across the bay and towards the You Yangs mountain range north of Geelong.

An historical attraction in town is the old steam-powered Portarlington Mill, which was built in 1857 out of sandstone, and now houses artefacts relating to the history of the region. Located within the Rotary Childrens Park at Point Richards is a miniature railway which operates at various times throughout the year

Nature reserve bush walk.

neighborhood_overview:
Moolap, Victoria, Australia
Moolap is a residential and industrial suburb of Geelong, Victoria, Australia. The name Moolap is derived from an Aboriginal word for nearby Point Henry, "moo-laa", thought to mean 'men gathering to go fishing'.

Moolap is a large but sparsely populated suburb used for agriculture, industry and low-density residential development. It spreads from Point Henry and Corio Bay across the Bellarine Highway to Reedy Lake in the south. Reedy Lake is a state game reserve. There is also a wildlife reserve on the eastern flank of Point Henry. The land around Reedy Lake supports an 18-hole golf course.

This is a very quiet property on the border of Jan Juc and Bellbrae.
A true 'bush meets beach' getaway.
Located very close to Sun Set strip, so an easy stroll into Jan Juc.
We are always walking or riding to visit friends/catch the bus/go to the beach in Jan Juc etc.
We are located exactly halfway between Jan Juc beach and Bells Beach.
They are only a 4-5 min drive away or a scenic 30min walk.
Jan Juc creek runs through our property, and then through Jan Juc, which has a wonderful reserve running all the way to the beach, along the creek.

host_about:
Hello!
I love my little piece of paradise 'Driftwood', where you can look out to the ocean and enjoy the beauty and serenity. Just footsteps down to the beach, where you can walk for miles in either direction or until your heart's content. There is nothing better than the walk along the beach to the jetty and into town for a delicious coffee at one of the many wonderful cafes.

The bay is an amazing spot all year round with many tourist attractions right at your doorstep. Some of my favourite activities include a trip up to Mariners Lookout, or Barham Paradise Scenic Reserve, where you can enjoy a babbling brook and admire magnificent eucalyptus blackwoods and myrtle trees. Maits Rest Rainforest Walk is another fantastic spot. As is the historic Cape Otway Lighthouse, the Otway Fly Treetop Walk and the Californian Redwood Forrest. At the end of a long day of activities, nothing beats the Great Ocean Road Brewhouse for a beer, cider or wine tasting with a great selection of local produce. Apollo Bay really does have it all! 

Whether it be a round of golf, surfing lessons, kayaking, a relaxing day at the beach with family, going on a tour recommended by the Information Centre, there truly is something for everyone. 

I so look forward to sharing my little retreat with you and your family.

description:
The Cove Beach House is nestled upon East Beach Port Fairy with stunning ocean views. Step out the back door and meander down a short path, to rest your feet on the sand. neighborhood_overview:
Uncover history in every corner of this charming fishing village at the end of the Great Ocean Road. The last destination on Victoria's famed Shipwreck Coast, Port Fairy boasts wide streets lined with nineteenth century cottages, great Norfolk pines and old stone churches. Join in the fun of the Port Fairy Folk Festival and buzzing local art scene, get active in the water, and see native animals in the wild, from southern right whales, seals and dolphins to wallabies, kangaroos and emus.

Take a walk down to the local port, one of the busiest fishing ports in Victoria, and watch as the fishermen unload their catch of crayfish and abalone. From the wharf you can head out to sea on a guided fishing trip or take a cruise out to the seal colony on Lady Julia Percy Island. Keep an eye out for breaching southern right whales off Port Fairy's coast during the winter months, when the whales come in to mate and calve.

Try something new in the water during the summer months.

name: View from the Ridge -  Gadabanud Country
description:
Spend some time amongst the gum trees over the ocean atop the Ridge, just off the Great Ocean Road between Kennett and Wye River.
The house sits amongst the trees overlooking the ocean up on the Ridge at Kennett River. High above the stunning Great Ocean Road, you'll wake to birdsong as the sun rises over the sea and dappled light fills the space.


This listing is for the upper house, with multiple options for the amount of rooms and beds available (See below).
neighborhood_overview:
The house sits on the Ridge above Kennett River, Beach, Café and small township where you can stroll along the shore or up river into the beautiful Otway rainforest. From the café you can walk up a hill that is perhaps the best spot to see Koalas (other than our deck!) anywhere along the Great Ocean Road. There are houses on one side of the Ridge, but the other is beautiful National Park you can wander at your own leisure, too.
The Beach/River/Café are a 5-10 minute walk from the house, though the ridge is quite steep.
Wye River town ( beach, café, general store and pub) is a spectacular 5 minute drive.
Lorne and Apollo Bay can be similarly reached via spectacular Great Ocean Road about 25 minutes East and West respectively.
The rest of the Great Ocean Road is easily accessible and spectacular, and inland you can visit the town of Forrest, lake Elizabeth, Beech Forrest and the Redwoods, and countless waterfalls, hiking trails and other attractions.

If you're feeling more active, tee up a round of golf at the Ocean Grove golf course situated across from the jetty.

Continuing your walk along the Barwon River will eventually lead you to the main beach of Ocean Grove, which you can access by crossing the road at the caravan park. After a refreshing dip in the ocean, head to the Dunes Restaurant located on the main beach for some creative cocktails, beer, wine, and delicious food on the sundrenched patio. We highly recommend the woodfired pizza!

Lorne has heaps to do and enjoy but, also a great place to escape and go at your own pace. If you visit once, you will definitely visit again!

As the largest holiday accommodation provider in Port Fairy and surrounds, we the team at Hearn’s Port Fairy Accommodation are your holiday rental specialists. With 130+ holiday rental properties, we offer the broadest range of holiday accommodation options in Port Fairy.

Located along the magnificent Great Ocean Road, Port Fairy is a quiet enclave on the edge of the dramatic Southern Ocean. Soak up the historic charm of this bluestone fishing village, learn about Port Fairy’s rich maritime history, be enchanted by the heritage listed bluestone cottages or wander up to the historic Port Fairy Lighthouse on Griffiths Island.

Walk the wide open street with a fresh coffee in hand and find a handmade treasure at one of the many artisan boutiques. Take your time over brunch, lunch or dinner at one of our many cafes and restaurants and sample the region’s produce.

Indulge the romance of the wooden boats bobbing along the picturesque Moyne River or take a long afternoon meander along the boardwalk. Take a long stroll along the iconic East Beach or explore secluded beaches and rock pools along the shores of South Beach.

There is nothing better than fresh air, good food and nature to nourish the body and soul! Port Fairy is the perfect retreat!

Contact the team today – your Port Fairy holiday awaits you.

description:
Enjoy our home with lots of space for family fun. Keep the kids active in the swimming pool, or get them to shoot some hoops while you relax in the mineral spa.

Take a short walk to the river or the local beaches, cast a line for a fish or go for a paddle, or just have a wander through the town. It's all walking distance in Barwon Heads.
